whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the Marketing Cloud Intelligence AP exam?

personas.label: Marketing analytics teams
personas.description: You report on campaign and media results and want to show that you can configure Marketing Cloud Intelligence.

personas.label: Marketing data consultants
personas.description: You help customers bring data from multiple marketing platforms into one reporting environment.

personas.label: Business intelligence analysts
personas.description: You understand data models and dashboards and want to apply those skills to marketing analytics.

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the Marketing Cloud Intelligence AP exam?
examDifficulty.summary: This is a moderate exam. Data integration and modeling are the more challenging topics: importing data, mapping it to the shared model, and ensuring metrics aggregate correctly. Dashboard questions tend to focus on basic reporting choices.
bullets: 40 scored questions in 90 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
60% to pass, which is 24 correct answers out of 40.
Data preparation. Review streams, field mapping, harmonization, and metric aggregation.
Reporting. Know dashboards, widgets, filters, and calculated measures.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Hands-on experience connecting advertising platforms and building a cross-channel dashboard helps. Aim for at least 75% on practice tests before booking.

examFormat.heading: Marketing Cloud Intelligence AP exam format
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are delivered online. Many questions describe a data or reporting problem:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: A scenario may show inconsistent campaign names across platforms or totals that seem too high. Identify whether the issue is data ingestion, mapping, harmonization, or aggregation.
bestWayToPass: Understand data streams: Learn how connectors and files load data and how streams are scheduled.
Map source fields correctly: Place each incoming field into the right dimension or measurement.
Harmonize platform values: Use shared keys or rules to align equivalent campaigns and other data.
Check aggregation: Additive metrics can be summed; rates need to be recalculated from their component values.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers Marketing Cloud Intelligence data integration and reporting, including workspaces, data streams, field mapping, harmonization, calculated measures, dashboards, and data monitoring. Check Salesforce’s current guide for the question count, time, and passing score.

keyConcepts.h2: Marketing Cloud Intelligence: concepts to review

blocks.heading: Platform structure and data model
blocks.body: Marketing Cloud Intelligence combines marketing data from sources such as advertising platforms, web analytics, email, and CRM for shared reporting. Workspaces can separate brands or clients. The common data model uses dimensions to describe data, such as campaign, channel, or date, and measurements to quantify it, such as spend, clicks, or conversions. Mapping data into this model allows comparison across channels in one dashboard.

blocks.heading: Streams and harmonization
blocks.body: A data stream brings in information through a built-in connector or file. During setup, map each source field to a dimension or measurement. Harmonization aligns values that represent the same thing across sources; for example, different campaign names can be linked with a shared key or naming rule. Classification rules can also derive dimensions, such as product line, from a campaign name.

blocks.heading: KPIs and calculated measures
blocks.body: Calculated measurements combine existing values to create metrics such as cost per acquisition or return on ad spend. Calculated dimensions group or relabel values. Aggregation must match the metric: spend and clicks can be summed, while a rate such as click-through rate should be recalculated from total clicks and impressions. Incorrect aggregation can make totals misleading. Insight features can flag unusual changes in key values.

blocks.heading: Dashboards and visualizations
blocks.body: Dashboards contain pages and widgets such as charts, tables, and single-value tiles. Filters narrow results by date, channel, or campaign. Start with the question the viewer needs answered and include only relevant views. Share dashboards with the intended users and schedule email delivery when regular updates are needed. Pivot-style tables can help analysts explore data before choosing dashboard views.

blocks.heading: Automation and integrations
blocks.body: Schedule data streams to keep reports current. If a built-in connector is unavailable, use supported file or API ingestion. Marketing Cloud Intelligence data can also be shared with Salesforce or a warehouse. Monitor stream runs and alert on failures; an unnoticed failure can leave incomplete reporting.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Marketing Cloud Intelligence AP exam
scenarioTips.intro: When a report looks wrong, determine whether the cause is the source data, field mapping, harmonization, or aggregation.

blocks.heading: Use streams and connectors
blocks.body: Choose a built-in connector when available and schedule streams to keep information current.

blocks.heading: Map and harmonize data
blocks.body: Map each field to the correct dimension or measurement. Use common keys to align matching campaigns across platforms.

blocks.heading: Build calculated measures
blocks.body: Use calculated measurements for KPIs such as cost per acquisition. Recalculate rates from their component totals.

blocks.heading: Design for the viewer
blocks.body: Start with the reporting question. Use filters to narrow results instead of duplicating similar dashboard pages.

blocks.heading: Monitor data quality
blocks.body: Use automated insights and alerts to notice sudden metric changes or failed data loads.

sampleQuestions.question: The same campaign appears as “Spring_Sale_US” in Google Ads and “US Spring Sale” in Meta. The team needs a combined result. What should it do?
options: Harmonize both names to one campaign key
Standardize campaign names and link them with a shared key
Remove one of the data streams
sampleQuestions.explanation: Harmonization maps equivalent values from different sources to the same campaign for combined reporting.
whyWrong: Manual renaming is difficult to maintain and can be inconsistent.
Separate reporting does not provide the requested combined view.
Removing a stream would discard useful data.

sampleQuestions.question: A dashboard sums click-through rates across campaigns and shows 340%. What is the likely problem?
options: There are too many dashboard widgets
The date filter uses the wrong field
sampleQuestions.explanation: A rate should be recalculated from the summed clicks and impressions, not added across campaigns.
whyWrong: Widget count does not change the rate calculation.
Late data does not explain summing rates above 100%.
A date filter would not make summed rates mathematically valid.

sampleQuestions.question: When a data stream is configured, what should happen to each incoming source field?
options: Add it to a dashboard before mapping
Rename it in the source system
sampleQuestions.explanation: Mapping aligns source fields to the shared data model so reports can use them consistently.
whyWrong: Unmapped fields are not ready for standard reporting.
Fields must be modeled before they can be used in a dashboard.
Source field renaming is not required for mapping.

sampleQuestions.question: Which item is a measurement rather than a dimension?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Spend is a numeric value that can be measured or aggregated.
whyWrong: Campaign name describes the data and is a dimension.
Country describes where activity occurred and is a dimension.
Channel categorizes the source and is a dimension.

sampleQuestions.question: The team needs cost per acquisition by channel. What should it create?
options: A new data stream for the advertising platform
A calculated measurement using spend and conversions
A filter on the campaign field
A separate workspace for each channel
sampleQuestions.explanation: A calculated measurement can divide spend by conversions to produce the KPI.
whyWrong: A new stream ingests data but does not calculate the metric.
Filters select data; they do not create a KPI.
Workspaces organize data and are not needed for this calculation.

sampleQuestions.question: Campaign names use the pattern “BRAND_PRODUCT_COUNTRY.” The team wants to create a Product dimension from the names. What should it configure?
options: Require every platform team to add a product field to its files
Use a classification rule to extract the product value
sampleQuestions.explanation: A classification rule can identify values in a naming pattern and create a dimension.
whyWrong: Manual changes across every source are harder to maintain.
A workspace organizes data but does not parse campaign names.
Filters select existing values; they do not create a dimension.

sampleQuestions.question: Reports are outdated because users forget to upload last week’s file. What should change?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A scheduled stream updates data without relying on a manual upload.
whyWrong: Widgets display data but do not load it.
Less frequent uploads would make freshness worse.
Deleting the dashboard does not address ingestion.

sampleQuestions.question: An agency serves three clients, and each client must have separate data and access. How should the account be organized?
options: Use a separate widget for each client
Use a shared dashboard filter as the only control
Combine all clients in one data stream
Create a separate workspace for each client
sampleQuestions.explanation: Separate workspaces keep each client’s data and configuration isolated.
whyWrong: Widgets do not control client data access.
A user-facing filter is not an adequate security boundary.
Combining client data in one stream weakens separation.

sampleQuestions.question: A data stream failed overnight and no one noticed for a week. What should the team add?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Monitoring and alerts can notify the team when a load fails so they can correct missing data.
whyWrong: A KPI does not monitor ingestion status.
Filters do not detect failed loads.
Dashboard size does not identify a data stream failure.

sampleQuestions.question: A dashboard viewer wants last month’s results for the email channel. What should they use?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Filters narrow existing dashboard data without creating new sources or pages.
whyWrong: A new stream is not required to view existing information.
A calculated measure creates a metric rather than restricting the view.
A workspace is unnecessary for filtering a dashboard.

sampleQuestions.question: A small advertising platform has no built-in connector. How can its data be ingested?
options: Copy it into a dashboard widget
Use a file or API stream
Assume the data cannot be used
Type values into a dashboard tile
sampleQuestions.explanation: File and API ingestion can support sources without a built-in connector.
whyWrong: Widgets display data but do not store source records.
A missing connector does not prevent file or API ingestion.
Dashboard tiles are not an ingestion method.

sampleQuestions.question: Why bring marketing data from several platforms into a shared model?
options: To compare results across channels in one place
To keep each platform’s report definitions different
To make dashboards load more slowly
To prevent the source data from being used elsewhere
sampleQuestions.explanation: A shared model makes compatible measures and dimensions comparable across sources.
whyWrong: The goal is consistent comparison rather than different definitions.
Dashboard speed is not the reason to centralize data.
A shared model does not require disabling other uses of source data.

sampleQuestions.question: Conversions double after a second stream is added, and both sources report the same events. What should the analyst investigate?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The same conversions may be counted twice. Determine the authoritative source or remove duplicates.
whyWrong: Workspace size does not double conversion totals.
Page count does not change how events are counted.
Color has no effect on metric totals.

sampleQuestions.question: Leaders want an alert when cost per click rises unexpectedly. What should be configured?
options: Review the dashboard only once a quarter
sampleQuestions.explanation: Automated insights or alerts can identify unusual changes so the team can respond promptly.
whyWrong: Removing the KPI hides the issue.
More data streams do not monitor the metric by themselves.
Quarterly review may be too late to respond.

sampleQuestions.question: What should guide the design of a Marketing Cloud Intelligence dashboard?
options: Every widget available in the tool
The size of the largest data stream
sampleQuestions.explanation: Dashboard content should support the decisions and questions of its viewers.
whyWrong: Visual styling follows the reporting purpose.
Too many widgets can make results difficult to interpret.
Source volume alone does not determine what belongs on a dashboard.
